card.name: Kwassa kwassa
card.tagline: Hips back-and-forth, hands following - the soukous craze
card.profile: Kwassa kwassa is a Congolese (DR Congo) dance and the fast soukous style it accompanies, emerging in the 1980s. Per Wikipedia, the dance was created by Jeanora, a Kinshasa mechanic, who mimicked the motion of a gearshift; the hips move back and forth while the hands follow the hips. It was globally popularised through the music videos of Paris-based soukous star Kanda Bongo Man, who restructured soukous with guitar solos after every verse rather than only at the song's end.
card.insight: Kwassa kwassa carried Congolese soukous to dancefloors across Africa and the diaspora in the late 1980s, and the term later entered global pop culture (Wikipedia; African Music Library).
